title: How Much Is Microsoft Office? 2026 Price Guide
summary: Microsoft office price 2026 starts at $179.99 for Home 2024 or $99.99 yearly for Personal, which includes cloud storage and automatic updates.
body_markdown:
## Hidden costs and limits of Microsoft Office plans


The limits that bite are specific to who bought. A one-time Office license gives no cloud storage and no feature updates, and Microsoft 365 Business Basic gives no desktop apps.


### Microsoft Office desktop apps missing on cheaper plans


Open Business Basic and you get the web and mobile versions of Word, Excel and PowerPoint, plus Teams and cloud services, but not the installed desktop apps. That suits a seat that only reads, comments and edits lightly, such as a front-desk or warehouse account.


It's a bad fit for the person who builds financial models, runs long mail merges or works offline on a flight, because the browser versions cover fewer features.


### Storage and device limits


Buy Office once and it installs the apps on a single computer, with no cloud storage.


That's fine for a solo buyer with one machine and stable needs. It's a poor deal for anyone who works across a laptop, a phone and a tablet, or who expects shared files, because you'd have to supply storage and sync yourself.


The allowance is finite. Subscriptions bundle OneDrive storage, but a seat that stores large project files, scans or media will hit it, and extra storage is a separate charge.


### Copilot add-on costs for Microsoft Office plans


On the standard plans, Copilot, Microsoft's AI assistant inside the Office apps, is included in the base price, with usage limits. Business customers add it per seat as its own license, so the real price of an AI-enabled seat is the plan plus the add-on.


The paid Microsoft 365 Copilot license is $30 per user per month. **Business Standard at $14 plus Copilot at $30** comes to $44 per user per month, or $528 a year, a little over three times the cost of the plan alone.


Across ten seats, that is $440 a month if everyone gets it, against $140 for the plan by itself. Give it to three heavy users and leave the other seven on the base plan, and the bill is $230 a month.


Buy it for the people who draft, summarize and analyze all day, and leave it off the seats that open a spreadsheet twice a week.


### Microsoft Office commitment and renewal terms


If a contractor leaves in March, you're still paying for that seat through the term. Business plans are typically sold on monthly or annual terms, and the annual term usually carries the lower per-seat rate.


With stable teams and predictable headcount, annual billing is the fit. Monthly suits seasonal or project-based staffing, even at a higher rate per seat. Also check auto-renewal before the term ends, since unused seats renew along with the used ones.
